place: Plain north of Capua; Aulius's house
scene: The morning after the twine. What Laberius did is shown by what is true at first light: two households on one plot
what_changes: Laberius has a promise he made to a farmer and a plot he has signed for, and they cannot both be kept
reader_knows_by_end: The land in the eighteen cities is assigned, compensation is not dated, and the veteran and the farmer both have tablets
pov_lens: Notices the farmer's hands and the old man who does not get up; misreads it as a matter between two men; hides from Vibius what he said yesterday

scene: Nysa's first weeks: one lamp, plain wool, a door where the dispossessed wait with their papers. Claudia, the young wife, in the house
what_changes: Nysa is given the door to count; she finds she knows one face in the queue from the Carinae
reader_knows_by_end: Octavian's house is poor in show and rich in petitioners; his wife is Fulvia's daughter
pov_lens: Notices who waits how long; misreads her new house as safer than the old; hides that she knows Fulvia's woman

scene: The dispossessed crowd into Rome with women and children. Octavian goes out to them and explains that he cannot help
what_changes: Octavian learns that explaining is worse than silence; he stops doing it
reader_knows_by_end: Why the land is being taken (the army must be paid) and why nobody can pay for it
pov_lens: Notices which of the crowd are farmers and which are hired; misreads anger as something that can be managed; hides that he was ill again that morning

scene: Manius brings Antony's interests and his own; Lucius is restless; Fulvia takes Antony's children to the soldiers
what_changes: Fulvia decides to delay the colonies until Antony's veterans are seen to be settled by Antony's people
reader_knows_by_end: Antony is in the East and not writing; Fulvia and Lucius hold his interests in Italy
pov_lens: Notices whose soldiers salute the children; misreads the soldiers' warmth as loyalty; hides that Antony has not written

scene: Allotment tablets offered as security. Bucco buys them at a discount; a dispossessed farmer offers Hordeonius his old title
what_changes: Hordeonius makes the first loan of his life against land nobody owns yet
reader_knows_by_end: Paper in the land war: titles, allotments, compensation, all undated
pov_lens: Notices the seal on the allotment and the date that is not there; misreads the war as a market; hides that he is frightened of Bucco

scene: Lucius as consul hears the dispossessed and finds he believes them. He writes to his brother
what_changes: Lucius commits himself in public to the farmers' side
reader_knows_by_end: Lucius is consul, Antony's brother, and sincere; his speeches are better than his plans
pov_lens: Notices crowds and whether they are his; misreads cheering as strength; hides that he does not know what Marcus wants

scene: Veterans further up the plain take more than their stakes. The scar-lipped man and the vine. Aulius's son and a pitchfork
what_changes: Laberius stands between a veteran and a farmer's son and finds he has picked a side without choosing
reader_knows_by_end: The settlement is turning violent across Italy
pov_lens: Notices who is on whose left; misreads it as a brawl; hides that he struck a veteran

place: Rome: the young Caesar's house; the Carinae door
scene: Octavian sends Claudia back to her mother. Nysa packs for her and carries the bundle
what_changes: Nysa stands at the Carinae door again, for the other house; Fulvia's woman sees her
reader_knows_by_end: The two houses are now openly at odds
pov_lens: Notices what Claudia packs and what she leaves; misreads the errand as housework; hides that she was glad to see the old kitchen

scene: Claudia comes home. Fulvia receives her daughter and the message that comes with her
what_changes: Fulvia stops thinking of Octavian as a sick boy
reader_knows_by_end: Octavian has publicly insulted Antony's house
pov_lens: Notices her daughter's face, then the messenger's; misreads the insult as weakness; hides that she was hurt as a mother

place: Rome: the theatre; the Tiber bank
scene: A soldier in the knights' seats; Octavian has him removed; the soldiers turn on Octavian's own centurion
what_changes: Octavian learns the veterans will kill for him and kill him; he gives them more
reader_knows_by_end: The army, not the triumvirs, is now the power in Italy
pov_lens: Notices the seats and who is in them; misreads the crowd as on his side; hides that he is afraid of his own men

scene: Lucius goes out to Praeneste with his guard; Fulvia follows him there, saying she fears for her children
what_changes: Lucius has left Rome as consul and become a party
reader_knows_by_end: There are now two sides in Italy
pov_lens: Notices the guard's numbers; misreads leaving as strength; hides that Fulvia decided it

place: Plain north of Capua; the colony forum
scene: Agents of both sides at the colonies. Octavian's men pay; Lucius's men promise. Vibius chooses
what_changes: Laberius's century splits; Vibius goes with Octavian's paymaster
reader_knows_by_end: The veterans follow the man who pays
pov_lens: Notices who has coin in hand; misreads Vibius as joking; hides that he is staying for the farmer

scene: Fulvia's silver-woman comes back, and this time she borrows
what_changes: Hordeonius lends to Fulvia's side against Fulvia's silver
reader_knows_by_end: War costs money; Antony's house is short of it
pov_lens: Notices the weight of the plate and the woman's hands; misreads the loan as safe; hides that he knew her face from Book 1

scene: Fulvia girds on a sword, gives the watchword and speaks to the soldiers
what_changes: Fulvia takes command of what Lucius started
reader_knows_by_end: Fulvia acts where the historians usually give women only influence
pov_lens: Notices which men look at the sword and which at her; misreads their cheering as an army; hides that Antony has still not written

scene: The house prepares for war. Octavian ill again; Nysa counts grain and arms in the storeroom
what_changes: Nysa is trusted with the count of what the house can hold out on
reader_knows_by_end: Rome itself may be taken
pov_lens: Notices how little there is; misreads Octavian's calm as confidence; hides that she gave Fulvia's woman the true number once before

scene: Veterans' officers try to make the two sides agree; terms are drawn up and broken
what_changes: Octavian learns that the officers cannot hold the men either
reader_knows_by_end: Both sides claim to want peace
pov_lens: Notices whose signatures are missing; misreads the officers as his; hides how much he has promised

place: Rome: the gates and the Forum
scene: Lucius enters Rome by night with three cohorts; Nonius opens the gates; Lucius speaks in the Forum
what_changes: Lucius holds Rome for a few days and believes he has won
reader_knows_by_end: The city changes hands without a battle
pov_lens: Notices the crowd in the Forum; misreads it as an army; hides that he has had no word from the generals

scene: Lucius's men at the door of a house whose master is away. Nysa answers it
what_changes: Nysa is asked to count for the other side, and does it, and tells nobody
reader_knows_by_end: Rome under Lucius
pov_lens: Notices the soldiers' boots and how many; misreads them as Antony's men she knew; hides what she told them

place: On the road north; the hills round Perusia
scene: Lucius withdraws north. Octavian, Agrippa and Salvidienus shut him into Perusia
what_changes: Octavian chooses a siege over a battle
reader_knows_by_end: Perusia is surrounded with ditch and wall
pov_lens: Notices Agrippa's markers; misreads the siege as safe; hides that he cannot win a battle

scene: Lucius in Perusia, looking north and east for the generals
what_changes: Lucius knows he is shut in
reader_knows_by_end: Pollio, Ventidius and Plancus are near and have not come
pov_lens: Notices the town's granaries; misreads the generals' letters; hides the count of the grain

scene: Laberius has come north after all. He digs the ditch round a town full of men he served with
what_changes: Laberius is on the line facing his own kind
reader_knows_by_end: What a siege looks like from the spade
pov_lens: Notices the soil and the distance to the walls; misreads why he came; hides that he left the plot in Aulius's care

scene: Letters to Pollio, Ventidius and Plancus. Their answers: they fall back to Ravenna, Ariminum and Spoletium
what_changes: Fulvia understands that no one is coming
reader_knows_by_end: Antony's generals will not fight Octavian without Antony
pov_lens: Notices each letter's seal and length; misreads Plancus's caution as delay; hides it from Lucius

scene: Sling bullets come over with words cut in them. Laberius reads one
what_changes: The war gets a voice, and it is obscene
reader_knows_by_end: Both armies insult the leaders by name
pov_lens: Notices the lead's weight and the cut letters; misreads the joke as about him; hides that he laughed

scene: Famine. Slaves eat grass; the dead are buried in trenches
what_changes: Lucius orders the slaves' rations cut
reader_knows_by_end: What the siege does inside
pov_lens: Notices the trench; misreads the townsmen as loyal; hides the order

scene: The night sally on the day before the Kalends. Laberius at the ditch faces men he knew
what_changes: Laberius kills, or does not, someone he served with
reader_knows_by_end: The sally fails
pov_lens: Notices the man on his left; misreads a face in the dark; hides what happened

scene: Grain prices in a hungry city; Sextus at sea; Bucco calls in veterans' loans
what_changes: Hordeonius forgives a debt and records it
reader_knows_by_end: Rome is hungry too
pov_lens: Notices the price of a measure of wheat; misreads his own kindness; hides it from Sosia

scene: Letters from the lines; a house of women waiting
what_changes: Nysa learns to read the camp letters' seals for news before they are opened
reader_knows_by_end: The siege is long
pov_lens: Notices which seals come back unbroken; misreads a delay as a death; hides her count of the dead

scene: News that Ventidius and Pollio wanted to fight and Plancus said wait, and Plancus won
what_changes: Fulvia gives up on the generals and decides to leave Italy
reader_knows_by_end: The relief will not come
pov_lens: Notices who brings the news and how fast; misreads Plancus as a coward; hides her plan to go

scene: Lucius asks for terms and comes to Octavian. They talk
what_changes: Octavian spares Lucius and decides what to do with everyone else
reader_knows_by_end: The war is over; the reckoning is not
pov_lens: Notices that Lucius is thin; misreads his frankness; hides what he has decided

scene: Lucius walks out
what_changes: Lucius is a prisoner who is called a guest
reader_knows_by_end: The surrender
pov_lens: Notices the soldiers lining the road; misreads their silence; hides that he is relieved

scene: Cestius, who calls himself the Macedonian, fires his own house. The town burns except the temple of Vulcan
what_changes: Laberius carries someone out, or does not
reader_knows_by_end: Perusia is destroyed
pov_lens: Notices the fire's direction and the temple; misreads the burning as looting; hides what he took

place: Octavian's camp; the altar of the Deified Julius
scene: The Ides of March. Men of both orders are taken somewhere. Laberius is not there. By night there are three versions
what_changes: Laberius chooses which version he will repeat
reader_knows_by_end: Some say three hundred were killed at the altar on the Ides; others say not
pov_lens: Notices who comes back and who does not; misreads a silence; hides what he saw on the road

scene: Fulvia flees to Brundisium and sails with Plancus
what_changes: Fulvia leaves Italy to find Antony
reader_knows_by_end: The losers scatter
pov_lens: Notices her children's luggage; misreads the sea as safety; hides that she is ill

scene: Laberius comes back to the plot. Aulius's family is there or is not
what_changes: The question of the twine gets its answer
reader_knows_by_end: What the war did to the land it was fought over
pov_lens: Notices the beans and the stakes; misreads Aulius's welcome; hides Perusia

scene: Departures and arrivals: Antony's mother gone to Sextus; Nero and Livia fled; Maecenas arranging a marriage with Scribonia
what_changes: Nysa is told to make the house ready for a new wife
reader_knows_by_end: The young Caesar is buying peace with Sextus by marriage
pov_lens: Notices what is moved out and in; misreads the marriage as a household matter; hides a message

scene: Fulvia finds Antony. He blames her and Manius
what_changes: Fulvia learns what her war cost her with him
reader_knows_by_end: Antony is back in the story, seen through her
pov_lens: Notices what he is wearing; misreads his anger as passing; hides that she is ill

scene: Calenus dies in Gaul. His steward's debt (Book 1 Ch 34) comes due to an estate that has gone to Octavian with his legions
what_changes: Hordeonius collects from the winner
reader_knows_by_end: Octavian has Calenus's army, Gaul and Spain
pov_lens: Notices the new seal on the estate's letters; misreads it as luck; hides the old debt

place: Rome; then the road to Brundisium
scene: Antony is coming with a fleet. Scribonia; Calenus's legions; Brundisium closes its gates to Antony
what_changes: Octavian goes south to meet Antony with an army that may not fight
reader_knows_by_end: War between the triumvirs is possible
pov_lens: Notices the soldiers' faces when Antony's name is said; misreads them; hides that he is ill

scene: Antony leaves Fulvia ill at Sicyon
what_changes: Fulvia's last scene
reader_knows_by_end: She dies here; the news reaches Italy
pov_lens: Notices the light and the sea; misreads his leaving as temporary; hides nothing any more

scene: Veterans of both armies at Brundisium will not fight each other
what_changes: Laberius sees the soldiers make the peace the leaders will sign
reader_knows_by_end: The army forces the peace
pov_lens: Notices the man on his left is Rufrius, or Vibius, across the ditch; misreads nothing; hides nothing

scene: Lucius, spared, at the edge of the peace that forgets him
what_changes: Lucius is sent away to an honourable post
reader_knows_by_end: The brothers' war is erased by the brothers
pov_lens: Notices that nobody mentions Perusia; misreads it as kindness; hides his relief

scene: Octavia's marriage to Antony. The household sews
what_changes: Nysa counts the wedding crowd, and the number goes to whoever asks
reader_knows_by_end: The peace of Brundisium; Antony married to Octavia; the Senate waives the widow's months
pov_lens: Notices the crowd and who is in it; misreads the peace as an ending; hides the count

scene: The final scene. Options in the storyboard README
